why: An agent resolving a meeting across offices. IANA names, which is what the schema description asks for. Note the JSON envelope itself is shared material: '{"timezone": "Europe/' is 21 bytes, so every European zone here shares a run longer than k with every other, before a single character of the value differs.
Second European zone, sharing the 'Europe/' prefix with three others.
Third, so the shared-prefix group is a group.
A different continent, so the prefix group is not the whole wave.
Second American zone. This server is a local control and is expected to egress nothing at all; if a timezone name reaches a network, that is the finding.
A short value on a third continent, to keep the wave from being two prefix groups.
All three fields required. Its argument set contains two values that appear alone in other calls of the wave, so it is ambiguous against both.
Same source, different target and hour, which is what scheduling across three offices looks like.
Two European zones in one call, differing from the call above in the source field only.
The shortest possible value. Three bytes of distinguishing material inside a shared envelope: unmatchable by construction, and the most common timezone an agent asks for.
